implementation_notes: scala.concurrent supplies the fan-out as a combinator: Future.traverse transforms a collection with an A => Future[B] function - documented as useful for a parallel map - and sequence turns an existing collection of futures into one future of results; firstCompletedOf is the first-to-settle policy (completed, not necessarily successful). Futures carry no timeout, so the budget is imposed at the edge with Await.result(combined, budget) or by racing the aggregate against akka.pattern.after, and each future must already be recovered if a single failure must not fail the whole gather. Aggregation is a map/fold over the successful values.
code_sketch:
import scala.concurrent._
val asks: List[Future[Offer]] = recipients.map(r => Future(ask(r)))
val gathered: Future[List[Offer]] = Future.sequence(asks)          // wait-for-all
val offers: List[Offer] = Try(Await.result(gathered, budget)).getOrElse(Nil)
val best = offers.sortBy(_.price).headOption                        // aggregate
pitfalls: Future.sequence and firstCompletedOf fail with the first failed future: without per-future recover, one bad recipient fails the entire gather.
Await.result blocks a thread and needs the implicit timeout; calling it inside a Future deadlocks small ExecutionContexts.
Futures start eagerly on the implicit ExecutionContext, so bounding the fan-out width means passing a dedicated bounded pool or a semaphore.

variants.name: Akka ScatterGatherFirstCompleted router
variants.implementation_notes: Akka ships the pattern as a router: the ScatterGatherFirstCompleted router sends each message to all of its routees, keeps the first reply and discards the others, and fails the ask with AskTimeoutException if no routee answered within the configured 'within' duration. The aggregate policy is therefore fixed at first-best-with-deadline, which makes this the shortest path when the recipients are already actors and the request is a message. What disappears is the partial-result merge: only one answer is ever delivered, so a quorum or wait-for-all policy has to be aggregated manually.
variants.code_sketch:
val router = context.actorOf(
  ScatterGatherFirstCompletedPool(nrOfInstances = 5, within = 10.seconds)
    .props(Props[QuoteWorker]()),
  "quotes")
implicit val timeout: Timeout = 10.seconds
val best: Future[Offer] = (router ? Quote(itemId)).mapTo[Offer]   // first reply wins
pitfalls: Only the first reply is observable: a slow routee is silently discarded, and there is no per-routee failure detail even though the timeout error mentions none of them.
within is the ask timeout too, so it must leave room for the reply to be processed by the caller, otherwise the answer arrives after the ask already failed.
The router is a pool/group over routees, not a general aggregator: recipient lists that change per request need RecipientList-style routing instead.
